record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Define the Harnack function Hz0 (z) for a Green domain D relative to z0 ∈ D to be the supremum of all positive harmonic functions h on D to be the supremum of all positive harmonic functions h on D which satisfy h(z0 ) ≤ 1. If Kζ (z) is the Martin kernel for D relative to z0 , K(ζ0 ) = 1 for all ζ in the Martin boundary ∆1 , then Hz0 (z) = sup{Hζ (z) : z ∈ D, ζ ∈ ∆1 }. In particular for D the unit disc, the boundary ∆1 may be identified with the unit circle T and, if z0 = 0, then Kζ (z) is the Poisson kernel with pole at ζ ∈ T . In this case, Kζ = H0 along the radius to ζ. Using the Riemann mapping functions, this property may be described for simply connected D as follows: for each ζ ∈ ∆1 , Kζ touches Hz0 along a Green line for D issuing from z0 . Does this property continue to hold for D multiply connected? (M. Arsove and G. Johnson)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a Green domain (a domain admitting a Green function), and fix a base point $z_0 \in D$. Define the Harnack function of $D$ relative to $z_0$ by
$$H_{z_0}(z) \;=\; \sup\{\, h(z) : h \text{ is positive and harmonic on } D,\ h(z_0) \le 1\,\}, \qquad z \in D.$$
Let $\Delta_1$ denote the minimal Martin boundary of $D$, and for each $\zeta \in \Delta_1$ let $K_\zeta(\cdot)$ be the Martin kernel based at $z_0$, normalized so that $K_\zeta(z_0)=1$. Then
$$H_{z_0}(z) \;=\; \sup\{\, K_\zeta(z) : \zeta \in \Delta_1\,\} \quad \text{for every } z \in D.$$
A Green line of $D$ issuing from $z_0$ is, in the simply connected case, the image under a Riemann map $\varphi:\mathbb{D}\to D$ with $\varphi(0)=z_0$ of a radius $\{r\zeta_0 : 0\le r<1\}$ of the unit disc $\mathbb{D}$; in general, a Green line from $z_0$ is an integral curve of the gradient field $\nabla g_D(\cdot,z_0)$ of the Green function with pole at $z_0$.

In the case $D=\mathbb{D}$, $z_0=0$, the minimal Martin boundary is identified with the unit circle $\mathbb{T}$, $K_\zeta$ is the Poisson kernel with pole at $\zeta\in\mathbb{T}$, and one has $K_\zeta(z) = H_0(z)$ for every $z$ on the radius from $0$ to $\zeta$; that is, $K_\zeta$ touches $H_{z_0}$ along the Green line from $z_0$ ending at $\zeta$. Using a Riemann mapping, the same touching property along Green lines holds for every simply connected Green domain.

Question: Does this property persist for every multiply connected Green domain $D$? Equivalently, for each $\zeta\in\Delta_1$, does there exist a Green line of $D$ issuing from $z_0$ along which $K_\zeta(z) = H_{z_0}(z)$ for every point $z$ of the line?
